title: Strong support
hookLine: friends, food, weather and places as strong supports of the mind

cards: Ananda, the Buddha's attendant, once came to him with what sounded like a generous thought. Half of the holy life, he said, is good friendship, good companionship. The Buddha's reply turns the thought around.
Don't say that, Ananda. It isn't half. Good friendship is the whole of the holy life.
A teacher who spent his life on the inner work of the mind, insisting that the people around you are not a side issue. The Patthana gives that conversation a technical name.

teach.b: The Pali is upanissaya paccaya, often translated decisive support or strong dependence. Some of the twenty-four conditions work between one moment and the next. This one reaches much further.
It covers anything that strongly inclines the mind, even from far back in time: a habit built over years, a teaching heard long ago, a promise you once made.
And the Patthana says plainly that it reaches outside the mind too.

teach.h: WEATHER, FOOD, A PERSON, A PLACE.
teach.b: It names weather, food, a person and a dwelling place as strong supports. An ordinary list: not rare insight, but whether you slept somewhere quiet, what you ate, the season, who you spent the afternoon with.
All of those lean hard on what the mind does next.

A strong support can tip either way. The same friend who helps one person be generous might, in another conversation, help them be cruel. A good meal can support clear practice; a heavy one can support sleep.
The condition isn't good or bad in itself. It's strong. That's why the Ananda conversation matters.
If a person is a strong support of the mind, then who you spend time with isn't only a social question.

teach.h: CHOOSE WHAT THE MIND LEANS ON.
teach.b: It's what your mind will be leaning on. The same goes for a room, a schedule, a plate of food.
Tradition says a meditator should look for a suitable dwelling, suitable food and suitable company before settling down to practice. That isn't fussiness. It's arranging the supports.

how: Buddhist communities give weight to spiritual friendship and to a suitable place, food and companions for practice, and Abhidhamma students learn this as the Patthana's strong support condition.

o: a teacher who must approve each practice
a vow to give the monks their daily food
something that strongly inclines the mind

p: half the holy life is good friendship
it's the whole of the holy life

s: a strong support is always a good influence
it's strong, not good or bad: the same friend or meal can tip the mind either way.
the Patthana names weather, food, a person and a dwelling place as strong supports
ordinary things that lean hard on what the mind does next.
the Buddha agreed that good friendship is half the holy life
he corrected Ananda: it's the whole of the holy life.

games.q: you're Ananda. you've just told the Buddha that good friendship is half the holy life. what does he say?
o: don't say that; it's the whole of the holy life
friendship is a distraction from practice
games.why: he corrects him upward: not half, the whole. the people around you are not a side issue.

practice: Look at the place where you're sitting: the light, the air, the sound, the chair under you.

If one small change would help the mind settle, like opening a window or moving a cup, make it slowly and notice whether the mind leans differently. If nothing needs changing, just notice what's already supporting you.

wordCard.voice: Strong support. The condition that strongly inclines the mind, from habits and teachings to weather, food, people and places. Today's word.

orig.note: Pali: strong support or decisive support, one of the Patthana's twenty-four conditions.

carryVoice: Your line: good supports. A friend, a meal, a quiet room: each one leans hard on the mind. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Samyutta Nikaya 45.2 (Upaddha Sutta), good friendship is the whole of the holy life
Patthana, the decisive support condition (upanissaya paccaya): climate, food, person, lodging
